raw.assessment: Full assembly plausibly reduces customer insertion work and exposes incompatibilities before dispatch; these benefits remain unmeasured. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting claims that full assembly inherently prevents the time target. Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, suggesting complexity or switching. Overlapping widths weaken a width-only insertion explanation. Missing-part reports and customer confusion remain separate failure signals. Diagnostic trials cannot establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Order-specific reusable staging trays may reduce mixed-batch selection and checking interruptions enough to retain full assembly.
openings.delta: Changes shared-bin retrieval while preserving assembled delivery; separates selection overhead from insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: Matched staged orders show lower total labor time and fewer retrieval corrections, with little insertion-time change.
openings.probe: Use 12 spare-board samples as six matched pairs across layouts. Alternate workers and condition order: current selection versus order-specific staging. Separately time staging, selection, insertion, checking, and packing, counting both workers’ labor. Independently verify packed components and color. Reject this explanation if insertion dominates or staging cancels savings.
assumptions: Reusable staging uses existing resources within the initial budget without recurring material additions.
Trials fit available time without delaying delivery.

openings.claim: An order-specific placement diagram may resolve short-partition uncertainty better than the current three-layout diagram.
openings.delta: Targets layout identification while retaining dimensions, compartment counts, exterior color, capacity, and removable partitions.
openings.prediction: With verified complete kits, customers using the order-specific diagram request less short-partition guidance and more often achieve their arrangement.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants to existing or order-specific diagrams, balancing layout difficulty. Record unaided arrangement within ten minutes, short-partition errors, and help requests. Treat results as screening evidence; verify replacement-diagram costs before deployment.
assumptions: The replacement insert stays within both cost caps and the delivery schedule.
Difficulty is partly informational; null results leave physical fit and other causes open.

raw.assessment: Synthetic observations motivate separate selection and placement hypotheses, without establishing causes. Combined timing and overlapping widths do not isolate insertion or dimensional tolerance.

openings.claim: Adapt double-entry bookkeeping: reconcile an accepted-order ledger of shapes, quantities and exterior color against parts staged on a reusable outlined board before assembly.
openings.delta: Accounting obligations map to required components; reconciliation maps to matching each shape and quantity. Failed correspondence: balanced totals can conceal wrong partitions. Changed material assumptions: physical identities require silhouettes and inspection; verify ledgers against existing templates. Shared bins feed a bounded staging area per order.
openings.prediction: If selection interference contributes, reconciliation reduces mismatches most in mixed-layout orders; unchanged insertion time would distinguish this from improved fit.
openings.probe: Use ten reusable sample sets in paired incumbent/staged trials, alternating worker and method order. Independently inventory contents and time selection, insertion, checking and packing. Include an equal-count wrong-shape substitution and uncommon colors; price setup and consumables.
assumptions: Staging fits the single bench and fixed schedule.
Verified order ledgers are accurate; costs remain within both caps.

openings.claim: Adapt a debugger source map: replace the generic diagram with an order-specific map linking illustrated partitions to destinations, emphasizing short-partition endpoints and orientation.
openings.delta: Source-to-runtime correspondence becomes part-to-slot correspondence. Failed correspondence: software locations are discrete; physical insertion also involves stiffness, friction and technique. Changed material assumptions: customers must recognize silhouettes without digital identifiers; placement information cannot correct mechanical fit.
openings.prediction: A placement-information cause predicts fewer destination questions and wrong-slot attempts, even if correctly targeted second insertion attempts persist.
openings.probe: Assign five participants per diagram condition, balanced across layouts. Record unaided arrangement success, destination questions, wrong-slot attempts and correct-slot retries. Keep parts identical; price preparation and printing. Treat this comparison as screening, then verify all pilot targets.
assumptions: Order-specific maps can be prepared within budget and deadline.
Diagram recognition transfers to customers without restricting later rearrangement.

openings.claim: Order staging may reduce selection interference; verified shape/quantity/color ledgers and silhouettes detect identity errors hidden by balanced totals.
openings.discriminator: Fewer mixed-order retrieval corrections/mismatches, unchanged insertion; insertion dominance or staging overhead defeats savings.
openings.fit: C1/C2 preserved; C3/C4 conditional on costs, bench space, accurate ledgers and deadline.
openings.probe: Alternate workers/method order in paired trials: Z1 six pairs/12 samples; A1 ten reusable sets, reusing within available resources. Time staging, selection, insertion, checking and packing across both workers. Independently inventory contents/color; include equal-count wrong-shape substitutions/uncommon colors; price costs.
openings.uncertainty: Representativeness/net savings unknown; preserves full assembly.

openings.claim: Order-specific part-to-slot diagrams emphasizing short-partition endpoints/orientation may resolve placement uncertainty.
openings.discriminator: Fewer destination questions/wrong-slot attempts despite persistent correct-slot retries distinguishes information from mechanical difficulty.
openings.fit: Preserves footprint, capacity, counts, color and rearrangement; cost/deadline feasibility unverified.
openings.probe: Randomize five participants per diagram, balancing layouts; use identical verified-complete parts. Record unaided success within ten minutes, help, short-partition errors and correct-slot retries. Price preparation/printing.
openings.uncertainty: Recognition/customer transfer unknown; diagrams cannot fix stiffness, friction or technique.

post_distill.decision: Screen both; causes unestablished. Full assembly may aid customers/expose incompatibilities; repeated orders approach target. Width overlap weakens width-only attribution. Synthetic small trials cannot certify 60-unit targets: >=98% completeness, <=8-minute median, >=90% unaided arrangement.
